Home › Strategy

Strategy on one page

11 November 2026 · Alexander Villax

Open every supplier conversation with pricing data, earn the listing second, and pair each new supplier with funded labs on the demand side.

Where GPU prices are heading

New-generation GPUs stay expensive through mid-2027 while older ones slide, and the gap between renting today and locking in for years stays wide. That gap is why the motion opens with Ornn for Providers: an operator's first question is what their capacity is worth against this curve. The full market note, with scenarios and signals to watch: GPU price outlook.

The motion

The first ask costs the operator nothing and gives them a private price benchmark. Each later step is a larger commitment that the earlier one has earned.

Who I would sell to first

Priority Profile First ask Why they say yes
1 Mid-size neoclouds and independent operators A private price benchmark through Ornn for Providers They price renewals with little reference data, and their lenders want contracted revenue
1 AI labs and model startups A reserved cluster for the next training run, with resale of unused hours They are over-reserved to stay safe, or waiting for capacity
2 Large neoclouds A data partnership and financing products, founder-led Tenant concentration, now acute as Microsoft trims its partners
2 Inference platforms and AI-native applications A price check on reserved capacity against the index and forward curve Rental prices move their gross margin

GPU lenders and trading firms go to the markets team with notes; GTM keeps selling capacity and data.

First 90 days

  1. Weeks 1 to 2: sit in on founder sales calls, read every closed and lost deal, learn the cluster due diligence process, and build tiered account lists of about 60 suppliers and 150 buyers.
  2. Weeks 3 to 6: run the outbound sequences in batches of 25 accounts per profile, testing which opening number gets replies, aiming for five discovery calls a week.
  3. Weeks 7 to 10: convert the first listings and reservations - write the qualification scorecard and objection sheet from real calls, and pass lender and fund leads to the markets team, and sign 10 GPU clouds to list capacity on Ornn and share their deal prices, so the index rests on more real transactions.
  4. Weeks 11 to 13: publish version one of the playbook with reply and conversion rates by profile, and propose the event calendar and product feedback for the next quarter.

How I'd measure it

  • GPU hours listed, and the share that fill
  • Gross transaction value
  • Days from first call to first trade
  • Active suppliers and buyers each month
  • Leads passed to the markets team: aim for 3 trading desks and 1 GPU lender in the first quarter

← 10. OdysseyGPU price outlook →
Home › Strategy › GPU price outlook

Where GPU prices are heading

My view is that a new generation of GPUs stays expensive through mid-2027, older ones slide as power and data-center space catch up, and the gap between today's rental price and the price of locking in for years stays wide. That gap is Ornn's market, so every operator, lab and lender needs that number, and Ornn is the only one publishing it from executed trades.

Where prices are now

All three main chips rose for a third straight month on Ornn's index.

OCPI, monthly average ($ per GPU-hour) Sep 2026 Oct 2026 Nov 2026 (to 15th) Change
B200 $7.26 $8.51 $9.67 +33%
H200 $4.89 $5.92 $6.84 +40%
H100 $2.83 $2.94 $3.26 +15%

H100 is back where it was in mid-2024 after falling to $1.63 in February 2026. Yet locking in for five years still costs a discount of about 49% on H100 and 61% on B200.

What drives it

Supply:

  • New chips are sold out - Blackwell allocation is largely committed into 2027 and advanced packaging at TSMC is still the bottleneck. Vera Rubin began shipping in August, with Nvidia expecting it to be about 20% of data-center revenue in its fiscal Q3, but early volume goes to hyperscalers.
  • The next systems cost more - GB300 and Vera Rubin systems shipping from early 2027 are reported to cost 15% to 17% more, mostly because of memory: a Vera Rubin rack carries about $2.0M of it against $374K for GB300, and server memory prices are expected to keep rising through 2027.
  • Power, not chips, is the real limit. Many sites cannot yet host Blackwell's liquid-cooled racks, which props up Hopper prices for now.

Demand: labs raised large rounds in 2026 (Chai $400M, Odyssey $310M, Generalist $200M) and will spend most of it on compute within 12 to 18 months. Inference runs all day, which turns bursty demand into baseline demand.

Financing: GPU-backed debt reached $48.4B in 2026 to 10 October, against $6.6B in all of 2025. Lenders push operators into long contracts at steep discounts, while neocloud shares have roughly halved in a month and Microsoft is trimming its neocloud partners.

Hedging has started - Hyperbolic bought a one-year put on B200 rental prices, covering about $5M of its rental revenue, arranged by Architect with Luxor as counterparty and settled on Silicon Data's index - meaning that GPU owners are now paying to protect against falling prices, and the first deals are custom contracts, not exchange trades.

Three scenarios for the next 12 months

Scenario Prices What would cause it
Base, my view B200 and B300 flat to +10%. H100 and H200 drift 10% to 20% lower by late 2027. The 5y discount stays above 40% Vera Rubin goes mostly to hyperscalers, memory stays tight, data-center delays ease slowly
Tight Every generation up 15% to 25%. Term discounts narrow Vera Rubin slips, the memory shortage worsens, another wave of large lab rounds
Loose Hopper falls 30% to 40%, Blackwell softens Hyperscalers release capacity, lab funding pulls back, distressed neoclouds sell GPUs

What it means for each buyer

Buyer Their problem in this market What Ornn sells them
Operators Selling five years at 49% to 70% off gives away the upside. Ornn's backtest found selling on demand beat a 40% discount in 97% of one-year periods Ornn for Providers to price against the curve, then futures to hedge
AI labs Prices are rising into 2027, and over-reserving wastes cash Reservations on Ornn Compute with resale, futures for big runs
Lenders Resale values are expected to fall sharply in 2027: H100 to 11% to 42% of list price Depreciation Curves and value protection
Funds and traders No tradable reference price for compute OCPI data now, ICE futures once approved

What I would watch for

  1. The five-year discount on Ornn's curve: if it narrows below about 40%, the market expects scarcity to last.
  2. Vera Rubin volume reaching neoclouds, and not just hyperscalers.
  3. Memory contract prices, the biggest driver of next-generation system costs.
  4. Hyperscalers releasing capacity, starting with Microsoft's neocloud review.
  5. Neocloud credit -> convertible issuance, GPU loan terms and any distressed GPU sales.

I inferred these titles from how neoclouds, labs and credit desks are organized publicly. The first 10 discovery calls should confirm or correct them.

How a decision gets made

  1. Supply (profile A): the commercial lead asks whether Ornn brings buyers they cannot reach themselves. The infrastructure lead checks that Ornn's standard and SLA fit their clusters. The CEO approves, and the CFO joins once lenders or value protection enter the conversation.
  2. Demand (profile C): the infrastructure lead compares price, hardware, interconnect and start date against two or three direct quotes. The CTO approves the technical fit. A founder signs once finance confirms the commitment fits the runway.

On supply, the CFO is the second door: a lender asking for contracted revenue or a floor on collateral value turns a listing conversation into a financing conversation. On demand, the fastest yes comes from whoever feels the capacity problem daily, and finance cares about resale because it turns unused hours back into cash.

Qualification criteria

Supply:

  • Owns or controls the GPUs, with the right to sublet or resell capacity.
  • Current-generation hardware (H100, H200, B200, B300) in a facility that can pass Ornn's cluster due diligence.
  • At least one block of capacity uncontracted in the next two quarters, or a contract rolling off.
  • A named person who owns pricing and utilization.

Demand:

  • Compute is one of the two largest cost lines.
  • Able to run on bare metal, Kubernetes or Slurm outside a hyperscaler, with no credits or commitments tying spend to one cloud.
  • A capacity need in the next 90 days, or an existing reservation that is larger than current use.
  • Funding or revenue that supports the contract size. Ornn pools tenants into rated baskets, so each tenant's credit affects the whole pool.

Playbook

I built the motion supply first: open with pricing data, then earn the listing, and then bring in financing, while demand outreach runs in parallel to funded AI labs.

Supply

Two reasons. First, capacity is still tight: on 10 November Ornn's index had the B200 at $9.90 an hour, up from $6.58 in late July, and the H200 at $7.24. Second, operators are under pressure: Microsoft is cutting back its neocloud partners, shares of CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN have roughly halved in a month, and borrowing costs are rising.

An operator in that position needs diversified demand and better pricing data, which is what Ornn sells. The first ask is access to Ornn for Providers, the second is a listing on Ornn Compute, and the CFO conversation about hedges and value protection follows.

Trigger events

Signal Side Why it matters Where to see it
Hyperscaler tenant cuts back or does not renew Supply Capacity comes free and the lender asks who replaces the tenant. Microsoft's November review touches CoreWeave, Nebius, ChronoScale, IREN, Lambda and Nscale Press, earnings calls, filings
New GPU-backed debt facility or equipment lease Supply The lender wants contracted revenue and a view on collateral value Press releases, filings, lender announcements
New site energised or cluster delivered Supply Fresh capacity is easiest to place before anchor tenants fill it Operator news, LinkedIn posts, power interconnect notices
Anchor tenant contract ending, or uncontracted capacity mentioned on an earnings call Supply A block of hours is about to need a home Earnings transcripts, investor decks
Funded startup cuts a product or team Supply Reserved capacity it no longer needs can be resold News, founder posts
Funding round of $20M or more Demand A new compute budget gets spent within a quarter Funding announcements
Hiring for infrastructure, compute or capacity planning Demand Someone is about to own the buying decision Job boards
Announced training run, model release or new research direction Demand A burst of demand with a date attached Company blogs, papers, X
Sign-up on Ornn's data site Both Someone is already checking prices Ornn's own sign-up list

Channels

In order of expected yield:

  1. Warm introductions through Ornn's investors and their portfolios.
  2. Founder-to-founder referrals from current customers.
  3. My own network: University of Chicago and Booth alumni, plus personal contacts across funds, trading firms and more.
  4. In-person meetings at infrastructure and AI events.
  5. The cold sequences on the Outbound page.

First 90 days

  1. Weeks 1 to 2: sit in on founder sales calls, read every closed and lost deal, and learn the cluster due diligence process. Build tiered account lists of about 60 suppliers and 150 buyers.
  2. Weeks 3 to 6: run the sequences in batches of 25 accounts per profile, testing which opening number gets replies. Aim for five discovery calls a week.
  3. Weeks 7 to 10: convert the first listings and reservations. Write the qualification scorecard and objection sheet from real calls. Pass lender and fund leads to the markets team with notes.
  4. Weeks 11 to 13: publish version one of the playbook, with reply and conversion rates by profile, and propose the event calendar and product feedback for the next quarter.

What I would measure

  • GPU-hours listed, and the share that fill
  • Gross transaction value
  • Days from first call to first trade
  • Active suppliers and buyers each month
  • Share of buyers who also resell
  • Leads passed to the markets team

Objections and answers

Objection Who raises it Answer
A marketplace will undercut our direct sales Supply You set the price and the terms. Ornn brings tenants your team does not reach, under one off-take contract, for hours that would otherwise sit idle
We are sold out Supply Then the conversation is about pricing the next renewal and the next cluster, which is what Ornn for Providers is built for. Listing can wait until a block comes free
Your buyers are startups. What about credit? Supply, lenders Ornn pools reservations from many tenants into one basket, so the operator underwrites a diversified counterparty in place of single startups. The structure is a conversation for the capital markets team
How do I know the cluster is any good? Demand Every cluster is evaluated to one standard and covered by one SLA and one support team. You see the site, hardware configuration and terms before you reserve
We can get a better price direct Demand Compare the quote against the index for on-demand capacity and the forward curve for term deals. Unused hours can be resold on Ornn
We are committed to a hyperscaler Demand Usually a disqualifier. Worth a follow-up only for burst capacity outside the commitment
Your index is conflicted because you run the marketplace Finance, large neoclouds The index uses executed on-demand rentals between verified counterparties, volume-weighted with outliers capped. The published methodology says neither Ornn nor its affiliates trade products indexed to it, and that trades on affiliated marketplaces get no preferential treatment. Detailed questions go to the markets team
Futures are not live yet Everyone Correct. Capacity and data are live today, and ICE has distributed reference settlement prices since 5 October. Hedging conversations go to the markets team

Cold-call script

The call has one job: earn a 20-minute conversation with specifics on the table. It should run under three minutes.

Opener

Hi [first name], it's [name] from Ornn. We have not spoken before. Can I take half a minute to say why I'm calling, and then you tell me whether it is worth continuing?

Reason for the call, supply

I work with GPU operators on pricing and placing capacity. We publish the compute price index ICE chose for its planned GPU futures, and we recently opened a workspace called Ornn for Providers that benchmarks an operator's prices against what the market cleared at.

I'm calling because [the new site went live], and operators in that position are usually deciding how to price new capacity and how much to keep out of long contracts.

Reason for the call, demand

I work with AI labs on compute. We run a marketplace where you can reserve GPU clusters for exactly the weeks you need and resell hours you do not use.

I'm calling because [you just raised], and that is usually when teams lock in more capacity than they need or get stuck waiting for it.

Questions

Supply:

  1. How much of your fleet is on long-term contracts today, and what happens to the rest?
  2. When does your next block of capacity come free or come online?
  3. How do you set the price for short-term hours right now?
  4. Do your lenders have a view on how much revenue needs to be contracted?

Demand:

  1. What are you running on today, and how was it bought?
  2. When is the next large training run, and how many GPUs does it need?
  3. How much of your current reservation sits unused in a normal week?
  4. Who else weighs in when you commit to capacity?

Competitive analysis

Ornn is the only company running the price index, the capacity marketplace, the hedge and the credit product together. Every rival covers one or two of those layers.

Why now

  • Rental prices kept rising: OCPI had the B200 at $9.90 an hour on 10 November, up 50.4% from late July, and the H200 at $7.24.
  • Neocloud financing came under strain: Microsoft is cutting back its neocloud partners, and shares of CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN have roughly halved in a month.
  • Listed futures slipped into 2027: CME's review now runs to 8 January, ICE has no listing date, and the FT reports that the CFTC is focused on manipulation risk in the benchmarks.

How Ornn pitches its products, and how I'd sell them

Ornn's homepage pitches one idea: "The market for compute. The index for intelligence." Below is how Ornn describes each product, who buys it, and what I would lead with.

Product In Ornn's words Who buys What I'd lead with
Ornn Data (OCPI) "Transaction-based GPU price benchmarks for the AI compute market." Built from settled trades, settles daily, on Bloomberg Funds, banks, lenders, operators, AI companies The free daily print as the door-opener; sell forward curves and history to lenders and operators
Ornn Compute "Buy and sell GPU capacity on Ornn Compute. Every transaction prints a real price." "Idle GPUs put to work." Operators on supply, AI labs and startups on demand Labs: reserve what you need and resell the rest. Operators: buyers your team does not reach
Ornn for Providers Launched October 2026 for select partners; not on the homepage yet Commercial leads at neoclouds and operators A free, private answer to "what is my capacity worth?"

Hyperbolic A GPU marketplace with software that standardizes mismatched clusters. About 250,000 users and $50M raised Developer self-serve Cluster-scale deals, where one SLA, due diligence, multi-year terms and financing decide the sale Strong with developers, and building its own resale grid
SF Compute Hourly reservations with resale rights. Says it has sold $245M of compute Developer-led The benchmark, the hedge and value protection on top of resale, plus a sales team The closest rival. Standard Intelligence buys through both
BGC Group OTC broking of compute and memory since June 2026 Existing broker relationships with funds Ornn publishes the price and can deliver the capacity behind it Brokers own the fund relationships. Better treated as a data partner
Barkr and American Compute Guaranteed GPU valuations backed by Munich Re, and residual value insurance with A- rated capacity Lenders and equipment finance firms Ornn sees rental income as well as resale prices, and can re-let capacity through its marketplace The hardest fight. Lenders trust rated insurance paper today
Nebius's own market Live spot prices, reserve auctions and a pilot rebate for releasing idle GPUs, since October 2026 Direct to its own customers Many fleets under one standard, and demand the provider does not reach itself Large neoclouds may decide they do not need a third-party venue

What this means for GTM

  • I'd lead with executed prices: Ornn's index comes from trades that cleared, while Silicon Data blends list prices, marketplaces and private deals.
  • I'd have a clear answer on governance: Ornn's methodology acknowledges that affiliates trade and deliver compute, and Silicon Data sells neutrality against that. The CFTC's focus on manipulation risk makes this the first question a financial buyer will ask.
  • I'd offer both legs: the physical-settlement camp argues that cash-settled futures leave basis risk. Ornn delivers real clusters and its futures settle against the same kind of trades.
  • Spend the sales effort on cluster-scale deals: self-serve players own single-GPU developers, while contract terms, due diligence and trust decide the larger sales.
  • Focus the next two quarters on spot volume and data adoption: nothing is listed on a US exchange yet, and that is true for every rival.

Before-event prep

  • Four weeks out, match the attendee, speaker and exhibitor lists against the target accounts. Aim for 40 named people and 15 booked meetings per tier 1 event.
  • Walk the floor and host one dinner. A table of six suppliers and six buyers, with index data as the content, suits a two-sided market.
  • Log every conversation the same day and send the follow-up within 48 hours, with the specific thing promised.
  • Let the markets team lead lender and trader conversations at SFVegas, FIA Boca and the infrastructure finance events, with GTM passing names in advance.
  • Measure meetings booked, meetings held, trades or listings started within 30 days, and cost per opportunity.
